title: Simple bots are visiting
what_happened: 858 visits (11% of all traffic) had no mouse or touch activity, moved through pages in about 0.5 seconds each, and kept almost perfectly even timing.
where: Top sources: social_x (520 visits), cheap_ads (124 visits), direct (123 visits).
likely_cause: Guess: simple scripts or attack tools that fetch pages without a real browser.
fix: Rate-limit or challenge these visits, and leave them out of your reports so averages stay honest.

title: Some visitors may be hiding as humans
what_happened: 535 visits were labelled AI agents. Another 347 visits (4.6%) could not be sorted with confidence and were marked Unknown.
where: Unknown visits by source: search (88), email (73), referral (68).
likely_cause: Guess: some Unknown visits are bots that copy human mouse movement and timing. Others are real people with unusual habits. This system cannot tell these apart for sure.
fix: Review the Unknown list, keep Unknown visits out of conversion numbers, and ask agent makers for a verifiable identity.

title: Scrapers are copying product pages
what_happened: 71 visits opened product pages one by one in number order, reading a median of 68 pages each at about 65 pages a minute.
likely_cause: Guess: someone is copying your prices or catalogue.
fix: Limit how fast one visitor can open product pages, and consider hiding prices from unknown visitors.

title: Sudden spike from social_x
what_happened: Between 2026-09-24 14:00:00 and 2026-09-24 14:30:00, social_x sent 452 visits. That equals 12.6 days of its usual traffic (about 36 visits a day). 72% followed the exact same path and 100% were judged not human.
likely_cause: Guess: an automated flood, possibly bought or fake traffic.
fix: Block or rate-limit this source for now, exclude the window from reports, and check any ads or posts that point here.

title: cheap_ads brings low-quality visitors
what_happened: cheap_ads sent 632 visits. Only 60% were judged human, and 91% of those humans left after one page. Its quality score is 23.4 out of 100, against a median of 72.3 for all sources.
likely_cause: Guess: the audience or the promise of this source does not match your site, or part of it is bot traffic.
fix: Pause or cut spend on this source until it improves, and test a different landing page for it.

title: Visitors pretending to be phones
what_happened: 192 visits (2.5%) claimed to be a phone or tablet but never produced a single touch. 98% of them were judged not human. The most common source was direct (57 visits).
likely_cause: Guess: bots that fake a phone browser label but run on a computer or server.
fix: Treat a phone label with zero touch as a strong bot warning, and challenge those visits.

title: Search-engine crawlers are visiting (usually fine)
what_happened: 265 visits (3.5%) openly declared themselves as search-engine crawlers.
where: Crawlers read many pages and never buy.
likely_cause: Guess: normal indexing by search engines. A declared name can be faked, so it should be verified.
fix: Keep these allowed, but verify them, and keep them out of human conversion numbers.

title: size_guide is a dead end
what_happened: 71% of human visits to size_guide ended there. Other non-checkout pages usually lose 22%, so this is 3.3 times higher. It was visited 639 times.
likely_cause: Guess: the page gives no clear next step, or it does not answer what the visitor came for.
fix: Add a clear next step on size_guide (a button back to the product or to the cart).

title: Many buyers leave at shipping -> payment
what_happened: Of 811 humans who reached shipping, only 289 (36%) went on to payment.
likely_cause: Guess: an unexpected cost, a long form, or a confusing step.
fix: Test a shorter shipping form, show costs earlier, and watch how many continue.

title: Visitors bounce between compare and product_detail
what_happened: 850 of 1,254 human visits that touched both pages (68%) went back and forth between them again and again.
likely_cause: Guess: visitors cannot decide, or they cannot find the answer they need on either page.
fix: Put the key comparison facts directly on product_detail, so people do not need to keep going back to compare.

title: Rage clicking on cart
what_happened: On 28% of human views of cart (432 of 1,516), the visitor clicked the same spot three or more times in a hurry.
likely_cause: Guess: something that looks clickable does not respond (for example a coupon or apply button).
fix: Check every button on cart for a delay or error, and show a clear response when it is clicked.

title: reviews is useful but hidden
what_happened: Only 1 page on your site links to reviews (rank 13 of 13 by links). Still, 87% of its 494 visits started right there, and visitors who saw it bought 1.9 times as often as the average human.
likely_cause: Guess: people search for it on their own because it answers a buying question.
fix: Link to reviews from product pages and the cart, so more people see it.

title: AI agents fail at payment -> confirmation
what_happened: At payment -> confirmation, 88% of humans continued but only 5% of AI agents did (humans: 289, agents: 259).
likely_cause: Guess: the form or button is hard for automated browsers to use, so customers who shop through an AI assistant cannot finish.
fix: Test the page with an AI browser agent, and make form fields clearly labelled and simple.

title: promo_ads visitors leave at deals
what_happened: 76% of human visits from promo_ads ended at deals, against 21% for visitors from all other sources (257 visits).
likely_cause: Guess: the promise made by this source does not match what the page shows.
fix: Make the deals page match the promo_ads message, or change the message.

title: Bots and agents distort your averages
what_happened: Counting everyone, the bounce rate is 19.0% and conversion is 3.6%. Counting only visitors judged human, bounce rate is 25.3% and conversion is 5.1%.
likely_cause: Guess: non-human visits are mixed into your normal numbers.
fix: Report on cleaned (human-only) numbers, and show bots and agents separately.
